description: A global dataset of multiple meteorological drought indices for 1961–2100 is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Jiachen Ji et al. Meteorological drought, characterized by atmospheric water deficit, poses widespread threats to ecosystems, agriculture, and water resources. While the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI), Evaporative Demand Drought Index (EDDI), and Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) are established monitoring tools, the scarcity of global-scale, long-term future projection datasets limits our capacity to assess drought risks in a warming world. Coverage: global; published in 2026. The formats are not stated in the sources read. The data are held in Zenodo and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support multi-sector infrastructure risk and planning studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
